summary: This benchmark note evaluates interchange interventions targeting the alias read and closing bracket tokens of a dictionary lookup within Qwen2.5-72B at layer 40. The empirical results show a near-complete null effect across 143 matched groups compared to a strong positive control in relocated declarations. The study provides exceptional precision in environment pinning and experimental parameters, although it remains a concise, single-site mechanistic probing study.
strengths: Rigorous experimental design incorporating positive controls (relocated declaration) and negative/constant-output controls across 143 dual-solved program groups.
Exemplary documentation of reproduction parameters, including exact model revision commit hash, hardware configuration, and pinned software dependency versions.
Careful isolation of intervention targets, testing individual token residual streams as well as joint token replacements at the exact residual dimension (8,192).
Preregistered evaluation criteria and strict thresholding (demanding rank 1 across the full vocabulary across four counterfactual completions).
weaknesses: Extremely narrow experimental scope limited to a single midpoint layer (block 40 of 80) and a synthetic dictionary lookup template.
Dense, abbreviated prose that omits in-line examples of the exact prompt structures and requires familiarity with prior unpublished iterations.
Does not explore multi-layer interventions or attention head patching to identify where the alias resolution mechanism actually executes if bypassed at block 40.
suggestions: Include a minimal concrete prompt pair directly in the text to clarify token alignment and counterfactual setups for readers.
Extend the benchmark sweep across multiple layers (e.g., layers 20 through 60) to map the causal trajectory of the lookup operation across model depth.
